subject: Post-stratification by time or time as a covariate?

messages.author: 06199470668a2843
messages.subject: Post-stratification by time or time as a covariate?
parts:
Hello list,

I am looking for some guidance on how to treat a time factor for a projec=
t
that involved repeat visits (with different line transects each time) to =
a
series of sites.
Background: I carried out bird surveys on 12 farms, arranged into 4 farm
clusters, with 10 repeat visits of 10 line transects each. The repeat
visits were spread over 2 years. I am chiefly interested in finding
cluster- and farm-level density estimates that are averaged over the
entire time period.

It seems that the two methods of accounting for the fact that the data
comes in 10 sets of 10-transect repeat visits each rather than 100
transects per farm at the same time (i.e. accounting for seasonal
variations in detectability), would be a) post-stratification by time
period, or b) adding time period as a covariate. I am not sure how
equivalent these methods would be. Specifically, I would like to avoid
having time period in the post-stratification slot, as practically any
analysis I run would need it there, and I thus would be unable to
post-stratify by any other factor of interest (e.g. geographic strata,
observer, sex). Including it as a covariate would leave me a lot more roo=
m
for customizing the analyses for other foci, but would the effect be
equivalent? I can't really come to a conclusion on that from the
documentation, and would value any input!

cheers
florian
